brief:
Tonight is Legs B, the last light night of the deload week and your sixth training day in a row. Tomorrow, Friday 25 September, is your rest day. The deload ends Sunday 27 September and Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.

Last night's Pull B came in at 31 minutes with every rep done. Where the card named a weight your machine doesn't have, you took the nearest real setting. That was right, so every weight tonight is one you have already used.

The numbers. RDL: 155 for 8, two sets, same weight every set, no ramp. Leg press, feet high: 140 for 10, two sets. Leg curl: 110 for 12, two sets. Abductor and adductor: 41 kg for 12, one set each, the same setting you used on Monday. Calf raise: 220 for 12, two sets, exactly Monday's numbers. Hanging leg raise: one set of 12. Cable crunch: 50 for 10, two sets.

Why the RDL and leg press aren't simply a fifth off your last Legs B: the RDL, leg press and calf sets on 17 September were all entered within seconds of each other, so they were typed in from memory after the session. I priced those two lifts off 5 September, which you timed set by set. That same slot on 17 September also holds kettlebell swings at 35 to 45 lb. That is almost certainly why the calf suggestion on Monday made no sense, as your note said. Tonight's 220 ignores it.

Every set tonight should end with plenty left in the tank. Rest, then Meso 3.

Two things still missing. Nobody has weighed you since 23 August (207 lb, 32 days ago) and the show is 158 days out. And your log holds one cardio session ever. Tomorrow's rest day is a good morning for a scale and a 20-minute easy walk.

flags.note: Deload week, day 4 of 7, last training night of the week. Rest day tomorrow, Friday 25 September. Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.
Tonight is your sixth training day in a row (19 to 24 September). Your plan runs six on, one off, so tomorrow is a rest day.

The RDL, leg press and calf entries on 17 September were typed within seconds of each other, so they were recalled after the session. Tonight's RDL and leg press are priced off 5 September, which was timed set by set.

The calf slot on 17 September holds kettlebell swings at 35, 40 and 45 lb, a different movement. That is very likely what made Monday's calf suggestion look insane. Tonight's calf number is Monday's own 220 for 12 and ignores it. Splitting the slot is a code change, not a Yes/No card.
Abductor and adductor read in kilograms: 41 kg is the setting you used on Monday. The app stores it as 90.39 lb.
Your RDL is on the stall list. Nothing gets chased inside a deload, so it waits for Meso 3.
On Tuesday's Push B you did overhead triceps at 45 for 9 when the card said 40 for 12. That may be a different cable at this gym. Not tonight's lift, noted for Meso 3.
Your recovery trainer read every note in your log by hand and found no pain, tweak or soreness. The automatic pain search is still broken: its only hit is 'number' matching 'numb'.
No bodyweight since 23 August, 207 lb, 32 days ago. The show is 158 days out and prep steers by that number.
Your log holds one cardio session ever: 15 minutes on an elliptical, 21 July. The plan asks for two to three easy sessions a week in build blocks, and Meso 3 starts Monday.
All three trainers reported. They agreed on six of eight lifts. The two disagreements were the calf raise and the leg raise set count, and both went to the recovery trainer. No vetoes.

proposals.why: You wrote "35kg is heaviest dumbbell" on 15 September and then shrugged it for fifteen reps on all three sets — the top of the range — the same fifteens you hit on 3 September. The weight has nowhere to go and neither do the reps, so this lift has no way to get harder in Meso 3. This opens the top of the range to twenty reps. The bottom stays at twelve, so tonight's deload card is unchanged either way.

overrides.reason: 155 for 8, two sets, straight across on the barbell. Your 185 on 17 September was typed in after the session, so I priced this off the 180 for 10 you timed on 5 September; 155 is a weight you have actually loaded for this lift.
140 for 10, two sets, down from the 170 you finished on 17 September. 140 is a setting you used with feet high on 5 September.
110 for 12, two sets. Your top on 17 September was 145; 110 is the setting you already did 12 with that same night, and it comes straight after the RDL on the same hamstrings.
41 kg for 12, one set. This machine reads kilograms; 41 kg is the setting you used on it on Monday 21 September.
41 kg for 12, one set, same as the abductor: the setting you used on Monday 21 September.
220 for 12, two sets. That is exactly what you did on Monday. It ignores the 17 September entry in this slot, which was kettlebell swings, not calves.
50 for 10, two sets, the same as Monday. 50 is the lightest weight you have crunched with at this gym; a lighter pin exists in your log only on other cable stations.

dissent.progression: 240 for 15, two sets — the lightest real calf-press weight he has logged at this gym (5 September), with the deload coming from the set cut.
dissent.recovery: 220 for 12, two sets — the nearest weight he has actually used, twice for 12 on 21 September.
dissent.why: It is a deload week and progression is asking for the heavier load, so the ladder hands it to the lower one. It also has the better receipt: progression's only objection to 220 is that 21 September was labelled 'Calf raise', but that is the most recent time he trained calves in this slot at all, three days ago, and 240 for 15 would be heavier and longer than that night. 240 is 20 lb under his 260 top; 220 is 40 lb under. On the week built to shed fatigue I take the one that sheds it.

dissent.progression: Hold — bodyweight, no numbers to set.
dissent.recovery: Cut to one set of 12, like every other two-set slot this week.
dissent.why: No weight is involved, and a bodyweight lift cannot carry an override, so nothing goes on the card either way. The app already prints one set of 12 on its own for this slot this week, which is recovery's position, so I record it as recovery's.
